candidates.module_text:
inductive TmS : Type
  | lit  : Int -> TmS
  | tvar : Nat -> TmS
  | add  : TmS -> TmS -> TmS

def evalTmS (env : Nat -> Int) : TmS -> Int
  | TmS.lit n   => n
  | TmS.tvar k  => env k
  | TmS.add a b => evalTmS env a + evalTmS env b

inductive StS : Type
  | svar   : Nat -> StS
  | sicc   : TmS -> TmS -> StS
  | sinter : StS -> StS -> StS

def memS (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) (x : Int) : StS -> Bool
  | StS.svar s     => senv s x
  | StS.sicc lo hi => decide (evalTmS env lo <= x) && decide (x <= evalTmS env hi)
  | StS.sinter a b => memS senv env x a && memS senv env x b

inductive PdS : Type
  | pmem    : TmS -> StS -> PdS
  | peq     : TmS -> TmS -> PdS
  | psub    : StS -> StS -> PdS
  | pseteq  : StS -> StS -> PdS

def denoteS (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) : PdS -> Prop
  | PdS.pmem e s     => memS senv env (evalTmS env e) s = true
  | PdS.peq  a b     => evalTmS env a = evalTmS env b
  | PdS.psub a b     => forall x : Int,
      memS senv env x a = true -> memS senv env x b = true
  | PdS.pseteq a b   => forall x : Int,
      memS senv env x a = memS senv env x b

theorem memS_svar (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) (x : Int)
    (s : Nat) :
    memS senv env x (StS.svar s) = senv s x := rfl

theorem memS_sicc (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) (x : Int)
    (lo hi : TmS) :
    memS senv env x (StS.sicc lo hi)
      = (decide (evalTmS env lo <= x) && decide (x <= evalTmS env hi)) := rfl

theorem memS_sinter (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) (x : Int)
    (a b : StS) :
    memS senv env x (StS.sinter a b)
      = (memS senv env x a && memS senv env x b) := rfl

theorem denoteS_pmem (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int)
    (e : TmS) (s : StS) :
    denoteS senv env (PdS.pmem e s)
      = (memS senv env (evalTmS env e) s = true) := rfl

theorem denoteS_psub (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int)
    (a b : StS) :
    denoteS senv env (PdS.psub a b)
      = (forall x : Int, memS senv env x a = true -> memS senv env x b = true) :=
  rfl

theorem denoteS_pseteq (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int)
    (a b : StS) :
    denoteS senv env (PdS.pseteq a b)
      = (forall x : Int, memS senv env x a = memS senv env x b) := rfl

theorem boolS_ext {p q : Bool} (h1 : p = true -> q = true)
    (h2 : q = true -> p = true) : p = q := by
  cases p <;> cases q
  . rfl
  . exact h2 rfl
  . exact (h1 rfl).symm
  . rfl

theorem pseteq_iff_mutual_psub (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int)
    (a b : StS) :
    denoteS senv env (PdS.pseteq a b)
      <-> (denoteS senv env (PdS.psub a b) /\ denoteS senv env (PdS.psub b a)) := by
  constructor
  . intro h
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    . intro x hx
      rw [← h x]
      exact hx
    . intro x hx
      rw [h x]
      exact hx
  . intro h x
    exact boolS_ext (h.1 x) (h.2 x)

theorem psub_sinter_left (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int)
    (a b : StS) : denoteS senv env (PdS.psub (StS.sinter a b) a) := by
  intro x hx
  rw [memS_sinter] at hx
  cases h : memS senv env x a with
  | true  => rfl
  | false => rw [h] at hx; simp at hx

/-
ROUND 3 -- the one requirement r2 left unmet: a free set variable is not
only a PREDICATE-layer atom, it is a BINDER, and the certified pipeline
decides a binder by SWEEPING its box-relativized domain.  r2 proved the
atom layer.  This round builds the binder layer, proves its sweep sound,
and then MEASURES the sweep's domain -- which is where the row's price
actually lives.
-/

/-- The decidable core of `denoteS`, box-relativized.  `psub` and `pseteq`
quantify over all of Int, so the sweep relativizes them to the box exactly
as the pipeline's box layer relativizes an ordinary binder. -/
def checkPdS (box : List Int) (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) :
    PdS -> Bool
  | PdS.pmem e s => memS senv env (evalTmS env e) s
  | PdS.peq a b => decide (evalTmS env a = evalTmS env b)
  | PdS.psub a b =>
      box.all (fun x => (!memS senv env x a) || memS senv env x b)
  | PdS.pseteq a b =>
      box.all (fun x => decide (memS senv env x a = memS senv env x b))

/-- The box-relativized denotation the sweep is actually sound for. -/
def denotePdBoxS (box : List Int) (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool)
    (env : Nat -> Int) : PdS -> Prop
  | PdS.pmem e s => memS senv env (evalTmS env e) s = true
  | PdS.peq a b => evalTmS env a = evalTmS env b
  | PdS.psub a b => forall x, x ∈ box ->
      memS senv env x a = true -> memS senv env x b = true
  | PdS.pseteq a b => forall x, x ∈ box ->
      memS senv env x a = memS senv env x b

theorem checkPdS_sound (box : List Int) (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool)
    (env : Nat -> Int) :
    (p : PdS) -> checkPdS box senv env p = true -> denotePdBoxS box senv env p
  -- `show` first: the target is only DEFINITIONALLY the equation, and
  -- instance search will not unfold `denotePdBoxS` to find the Decidable
  -- instance (the committed slice records the same hazard on
  -- `checkStmtBox_sound`).
  | PdS.pmem _ _, h => h
  | PdS.peq a b, h => by
      show evalTmS env a = evalTmS env b
      exact of_decide_eq_true h
  | PdS.psub a b, h => by
      simp only [checkPdS, List.all_eq_true] at h
      intro x hx hxa
      have hb := h x hx
      rw [hxa] at hb
      simpa using hb
  | PdS.pseteq _ _, h => by
      simp only [checkPdS, List.all_eq_true] at h
      intro x hx
      exact of_decide_eq_true (h x hx)

/-- The statement layer with BOTH binder kinds.  `sallS` binds an ordinary
Int variable; `ssallS` binds a SET -- the constructor the row's lead
subject (`09_Sets#definition-003`, an intersection of two sets the source
gives no comprehension for) needs TWICE. -/
inductive StmtS : Type
  | base : PdS -> StmtS
  | sallS : Nat -> StmtS -> StmtS
  | ssallS : Nat -> StmtS -> StmtS

def updEnvS (env : Nat -> Int) (k : Nat) (v : Int) : Nat -> Int :=
  fun i => if i = k then v else env i

/-- Membership in a first-order subset, by structural recursion.  `List.contains`
would read better and cannot be used: the compiler specializes it into a
constant of its own (`List.elem._at.FgReflect.updSenvS._spec_1`), which the
trusted replay's constant audit refuses for exactly the reason it refuses a
lifted lambda.  A whitelist is a trust root; the candidate is what moves. -/
def memL : List Int -> Int -> Bool
  | [], _ => false
  | a :: as, y => if y = a then true else memL as y

/-- The set binder's assignment arrives as FIRST-ORDER DATA -- a list of the
box elements the set contains -- and is decoded here.  The body is a lambda
in DEFINITION position, so it eta-expands into this constant's own arity and
no closure is ever lifted out of it. -/
def updSenvS (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (k : Nat) (u : List Int) :
    Nat -> Int -> Bool :=
  fun i y => if i = k then memL u y else senv i y

/-- Box-relativized statement semantics.  The Int binder ranges over `box`;
the SET binder ranges over `sbox` -- the list of set assignments the sweep
enumerates.  Soundness below is relative to exactly that list, which is the
whole point: the theorem is easy, the LIST is not. -/
def denoteStmtBoxS (box : List Int) (sbox : List (List Int))
    (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) : StmtS -> Prop
  | StmtS.base p => denotePdBoxS box senv env p
  | StmtS.sallS k s =>
      forall v, v ∈ box -> denoteStmtBoxS box sbox senv (updEnvS env k v) s
  | StmtS.ssallS k s =>
      forall u, u ∈ sbox -> denoteStmtBoxS box sbox (updSenvS senv k u) env s

def checkStmtBoxS (box : List Int) (sbox : List (List Int))
    (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) : StmtS -> Bool
  | StmtS.base p => checkPdS box senv env p
  | StmtS.sallS k s =>
      box.all (fun v => checkStmtBoxS box sbox senv (updEnvS env k v) s)
  | StmtS.ssallS k s =>
      sbox.all (fun u => checkStmtBoxS box sbox (updSenvS senv k u) env s)

/-- SOUNDNESS of the set-binder sweep.  It goes through -- so the tower is
NOT blocked by proof obligations.  What it is relative to is `sbox`. -/
theorem checkStmtBoxS_sound (box : List Int) (sbox : List (List Int)) :
    (s : StmtS) -> (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) -> (env : Nat -> Int) ->
      checkStmtBoxS box sbox senv env s = true ->
        denoteStmtBoxS box sbox senv env s
  | StmtS.base p, senv, env, h => checkPdS_sound box senv env p h
  | StmtS.sallS k s, senv, env, h => by
      simp only [checkStmtBoxS, List.all_eq_true] at h
      intro v hv
      exact checkStmtBoxS_sound box sbox s senv (updEnvS env k v) (h v hv)
  | StmtS.ssallS k s, senv, env, h => by
      simp only [checkStmtBoxS, List.all_eq_true] at h
      intro u hu
      exact checkStmtBoxS_sound box sbox s (updSenvS senv k u) env (h u hu)

/-- Adjoin `x` to every subset in a list.  Round 3 wrote this as
`(subsetsOfS xs).map (fun u => fun y => ...)`, and the trusted replay's
constant audit refused the result: storing a FUNCTION into a list forces the
compiler to lift the closure into a constant of its own
(`FgReflect.subsetsOfS._elambda_1`) and to specialize the map through
`List.mapTR.loop._at.FgReflect.subsetsOfS._spec_1`.  Neither is in the
measured whitelist, and the whitelist is a trust root rather than a knob.
Here `x :: s` is a CONSTRUCTOR application over first-order data, so nothing
is lifted. -/
def consL (x : Int) : List (List Int) -> List (List Int)
  | [] => []
  | s :: ss => (x :: s) :: consL x ss

/-- For the sweep's verdict to mean what the emitted `forall U : Set Int`
says, `sbox` must be EVERY subset of the box.  This builds it. -/
def subsetsOfS : List Int -> List (List Int)
  | [] => [[]]
  | x :: xs => (subsetsOfS xs) ++ consL x (subsetsOfS xs)

theorem consL_length (x : Int) :
    (ss : List (List Int)) -> (consL x ss).length = ss.length
  | [] => rfl
  | s :: ss => by
      simp [consL, consL_length x ss]

/-- THE MEASUREMENT, as a theorem instead of a paragraph: one set binder's
box-relativized domain is 2 ^ |box|.  At the committed Int box (2*8+1 = 17
values) that is 131072 set assignments for ONE set variable; the lead
subject needs two, beside an ordinary Int binder. -/
theorem subsetsOfS_length :
    (b : List Int) -> (subsetsOfS b).length = 2 ^ b.length
  | [] => rfl
  | x :: xs => by
      simp [subsetsOfS, List.length_append, consL_length,
        subsetsOfS_length xs, Nat.pow_succ, Nat.mul_two]

/-- And the sweep over that domain is what a set binder COSTS: the checker
folds `sbox` at every set binder, so a statement with `n` set binders costs
`(2 ^ |box|) ^ n` leaf checks.  Stated for the two-binder shape the lead
subject actually has. -/
theorem ssall_two_binder_cost (box : List Int) (k1 k2 : Nat) (p : PdS)
    (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) :
    checkStmtBoxS box (subsetsOfS box) senv env
        (StmtS.ssallS k1 (StmtS.ssallS k2 (StmtS.base p)))
      = (subsetsOfS box).all (fun u1 =>
          (subsetsOfS box).all (fun u2 =>
            checkPdS box (updSenvS (updSenvS senv k1 u1) k2 u2) env p)) := rfl

/-
ROUND 5 -- the one requirement r4 left unmet, and it is the sharper half of
the row's own class measurement.

`tests/test_set_carrier_box_domain.py::
test_the_forall_path_has_no_combinatorial_ceiling_at_all` measures, against
`generators/math_eval.py` itself, that `EXISTS_SHADOW_MAX_ASSIGNMENTS` is
consulted at exactly ONE site -- inside `exists_shadow_shape`, which returns
`forall-only` BEFORE the ceiling arithmetic.  So the pipeline's only
combinatorial ceiling guards the EXISTS path, and the FORALL path has none.

r4 built the set-binder sweep, proved it sound, and priced its domain at
`(2 ^ |box|) ^ n`.  What r4's checker does with that price is SWEEP IT
ANYWAY: `checkStmtBoxS` folds `sbox` unconditionally, so on this row's lead
subject -- `09_Sets#definition-003`, a DEFINITION (forall-only) with two set
binders, 292 billion leaf checks at the committed Int box -- it would not
answer and would not honest-skip.  It would run.

A verdict that cannot be reached is worse than a verdict of "too large":
the second is a reading, the first is a hang.  This round adds exactly one
layer -- a BUDGETED verdict -- and proves the two things that make it a
reading rather than a weakening of the gate:

  * soundness SURVIVES the budget (`checkStmtFuelS_sound`): a `some true`
    verdict still implies the box denotation, so the budget removes answers
    and never adds them; and
  * the budget is HONEST in the other direction
    (`checkStmtFuelS_none_of_over_budget`): over budget the verdict is
    `none` and never `some _`, so a skip can never impersonate a pass.

The cost is then tied back to the cardinality r4 already proved
(`lead_subject_cost_is_the_squared_powerset`), so the price is stated
against the same number the measurement uses rather than a fresh one.

WHY THE VERDICT IS `Option Bool` AND NOT A THREE-VALUED INDUCTIVE.  This
round was first authored with `inductive VerdictS | holds | failed |
tooLarge`, which elaborates and kernel-replays cleanly and still FAILS the
ride: its compiled form carries `lcUnreachable`, outside the measured
constant whitelist.  Bisected here rather than guessed -- three probes:

  * direct `Nat` recursion over `StmtS` (3 constructors, WITH fields): clean;
  * the parameterized cost function below, pattern-matched: clean;
  * the nullary `VerdictS` enum plus one `cond`: `lcUnreachable`.

So the rule is sharper than "avoid new inductives": it is the NULLARY-ONLY
enum specifically.  Lean unboxes an all-nullary inductive to a scalar tag
and its `casesOn` compiles to a jump table with an unreachable default;
`StmtS` escapes precisely because its constructors carry fields.  Rewriting
the definition through `StmtS.rec` to dodge the tree does not work either --
`code generator does not support recursor 'FgReflect.StmtS.rec'`, so the
definition has no executable code and every dependent fails the IR check.
`Option Bool` carries the same three readings with no new type at all:
`none` IS the honest skip.

That is the third instance in this lineage of one rule -- r4 records
`List.contains` specializing into its own constant and `List.map` lifting a
closure.  The whitelist is a trust root; the CANDIDATE is what moves.

BOUND, restated because it is the whole discipline here: this is a PARALLEL
TOWER and a PROPOSAL.  It adds no constructor to the committed `Tm`/`Pd`,
edits `tools/FgReflect.lean` not at all, and changes nothing about what the
Python gate does today -- `generators/math_eval.py` is untouched.  Whether
the pipeline should acquire a forall-side ceiling is a decision this round
PRICES and does not take.
-/

/-- The sweep's leaf count: an ordinary binder multiplies by the box, a SET
binder multiplies by `sbox` -- which `subsetsOfS_length` proves is
`2 ^ |box|`.  This is r4's price as a function rather than as a theorem
about one shape. -/
def costStmtS (box : List Int) (sbox : List (List Int)) : StmtS -> Nat
  | StmtS.base _ => 1
  | StmtS.sallS _ s => box.length * costStmtS box sbox s
  | StmtS.ssallS _ s => sbox.length * costStmtS box sbox s

/-- In-budget as first-order data, so the verdict below is a plain `cond`
and no `Decidable` instance has to be found under a definitional unfold --
the hazard the committed slice records on `checkStmtBox_sound` and r4 hit
again on `checkPdS_sound`. -/
def inBudgetS (fuel : Nat) (box : List Int) (sbox : List (List Int))
    (s : StmtS) : Bool :=
  decide (costStmtS box sbox s <= fuel)

/-- THE BUDGETED SWEEP.  In budget it is exactly r4's checker; over budget
it declines to run and says so.  `none` is the reading r4's checker
structurally cannot express, and expressing it is the whole round. -/
def checkStmtFuelS (fuel : Nat) (box : List Int) (sbox : List (List Int))
    (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) (s : StmtS) : Option Bool :=
  cond (inBudgetS fuel box sbox s)
    (some (checkStmtBoxS box sbox senv env s))
    none

/-- SOUNDNESS SURVIVES THE BUDGET.  A `some true` verdict still implies the
box-relativized denotation, so nothing certifies that r4's sweep did not
already certify: the budget subtracts answers, it never adds them. -/
theorem checkStmtFuelS_sound (fuel : Nat) (box : List Int)
    (sbox : List (List Int)) (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int)
    (s : StmtS)
    (h : checkStmtFuelS fuel box sbox senv env s = some true) :
    denoteStmtBoxS box sbox senv env s := by
  cases hb : inBudgetS fuel box sbox s with
  | false => simp [checkStmtFuelS, hb] at h
  | true =>
      simp [checkStmtFuelS, hb] at h
      exact checkStmtBoxS_sound box sbox s senv env h

/-- HONEST IN THE OTHER DIRECTION.  Over budget the verdict is `none`, so a
skip can never be read as a pass.  This is the half that makes the budget a
READING rather than a quiet weakening. -/
theorem checkStmtFuelS_none_of_over_budget (fuel : Nat) (box : List Int)
    (sbox : List (List Int)) (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int)
    (s : StmtS) (h : fuel < costStmtS box sbox s) :
    checkStmtFuelS fuel box sbox senv env s = none := by
  have hb : inBudgetS fuel box sbox s = false := by
    simp [inBudgetS, Nat.not_le.mpr h]
  simp [checkStmtFuelS, hb]

/-- And therefore it never answers `some true` over budget -- the form a
caller actually relies on, and the one that would have to hold before any
gate could adopt a ceiling. -/
theorem checkStmtFuelS_ne_pass_of_over_budget (fuel : Nat) (box : List Int)
    (sbox : List (List Int)) (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int)
    (s : StmtS) (h : fuel < costStmtS box sbox s) :
    checkStmtFuelS fuel box sbox senv env s ≠ some true := by
  rw [checkStmtFuelS_none_of_over_budget fuel box sbox senv env s h]
  intro hx
  exact Option.noConfusion hx

/-- THE PRICE, tied back to the cardinality r4 proved rather than restated:
the lead subject's shape -- two set binders over an ordinary Int binder --
costs the SQUARE of the powerset of the box, times the box.  At the
committed Int box (17 values) that is 131072 * 131072 * 17 leaf checks,
which is the 292 billion the Python measurement prices. -/
theorem lead_subject_cost_is_the_squared_powerset (box : List Int)
    (k1 k2 j : Nat) (p : PdS) :
    costStmtS box (subsetsOfS box)
        (StmtS.ssallS k1 (StmtS.ssallS k2 (StmtS.sallS j (StmtS.base p))))
      = (2 ^ box.length) * ((2 ^ box.length) * (box.length * 1)) := by
  simp [costStmtS, subsetsOfS_length]

/-- And so the lead subject's shape is over EVERY budget below its domain --
stated as an implication over the budget rather than at one literal, so it
prices the SHAPE and never a remembered constant. -/
theorem lead_subject_is_over_any_budget_below_its_domain (box : List Int)
    (k1 k2 j : Nat) (p : PdS) (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int)
    (fuel : Nat)
    (h : fuel < (2 ^ box.length) * ((2 ^ box.length) * (box.length * 1))) :
    checkStmtFuelS fuel box (subsetsOfS box) senv env
        (StmtS.ssallS k1 (StmtS.ssallS k2 (StmtS.sallS j (StmtS.base p))))
      = none := by
  apply checkStmtFuelS_none_of_over_budget
  rw [lead_subject_cost_is_the_squared_powerset]
  exact h

/-- COMPLETENESS -- the dual r5 left open, and the reason its honesty is not
vacuous.  r5 proved that OVER budget the sweep declines; on its own that is
satisfied by a checker which declines ALWAYS, so soundness plus
over-budget-honesty still permits a ceiling that answers nothing.  This is
the other half: a shape the budget CAN pay is never skipped, and what comes
back is exactly r4's unbudgeted verdict.  The budget subtracts answers only
where it cannot afford them. -/
theorem checkStmtFuelS_some_of_in_budget (fuel : Nat) (box : List Int)
    (sbox : List (List Int)) (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int)
    (s : StmtS) (h : costStmtS box sbox s <= fuel) :
    checkStmtFuelS fuel box sbox senv env s
      = some (checkStmtBoxS box sbox senv env s) := by
  have hb : inBudgetS fuel box sbox s = true := by
    simp [inBudgetS, h]
  simp [checkStmtFuelS, hb]

/-- And so the skip is EXACTLY the over-budget case: `none` characterizes the
price and nothing else.  With this the ceiling is a total function of what a
shape costs, rather than a licence to refuse whatever it likes. -/
theorem checkStmtFuelS_eq_none_iff (fuel : Nat) (box : List Int)
    (sbox : List (List Int)) (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int)
    (s : StmtS) :
    checkStmtFuelS fuel box sbox senv env s = none
      <-> fuel < costStmtS box sbox s := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    by_contra hc
    have hle : costStmtS box sbox s <= fuel := Nat.not_lt.mp hc
    rw [checkStmtFuelS_some_of_in_budget fuel box sbox senv env s hle] at h
    exact Option.noConfusion h
  · intro h
    exact checkStmtFuelS_none_of_over_budget fuel box sbox senv env s h

/-- THE TRACTABLE RUNG'S SHAPE: one set binder over one ordinary object
binder, the shape the class measurement prices as small at a smaller
carrier. -/
theorem single_set_binder_cost (box : List Int) (k j : Nat) (p : PdS) :
    costStmtS box (subsetsOfS box)
        (StmtS.ssallS k (StmtS.sallS j (StmtS.base p)))
      = (2 ^ box.length) * (box.length * 1) := by
  simp [costStmtS, subsetsOfS_length]

/-- AND THE SECOND SET BINDER COSTS A WHOLE POWERSET MORE.  This is the class
measurement's "two rungs wearing one name" as arithmetic rather than as a
pair of remembered numbers: the gap between the rung that answers and the
rung that cannot is exactly one factor of `2 ^ |box|`, whatever the carrier
underneath. -/
theorem the_second_set_binder_costs_a_whole_powerset_more (box : List Int)
    (k1 k2 j : Nat) (p : PdS) :
    costStmtS box (subsetsOfS box)
        (StmtS.ssallS k1 (StmtS.ssallS k2 (StmtS.sallS j (StmtS.base p))))
      = (2 ^ box.length)
          * costStmtS box (subsetsOfS box)
              (StmtS.ssallS k2 (StmtS.sallS j (StmtS.base p))) := by
  simp [costStmtS, subsetsOfS_length]

/-- THE TRACTABLE RUNG, ANSWERING.  At any budget that affords its price the
one-set-binder shape returns a verdict rather than a skip.  Paired with r5's
`lead_subject_is_over_any_budget_below_its_domain`, the two are the SPLIT:
same checker, same box, one binder answers and two do not. -/
theorem single_set_binder_answers_in_budget (box : List Int) (k j : Nat)
    (p : PdS) (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) (fuel : Nat)
    (h : (2 ^ box.length) * (box.length * 1) <= fuel) :
    checkStmtFuelS fuel box (subsetsOfS box) senv env
        (StmtS.ssallS k (StmtS.sallS j (StmtS.base p)))
      = some (checkStmtBoxS box (subsetsOfS box) senv env
          (StmtS.ssallS k (StmtS.sallS j (StmtS.base p)))) := by
  apply checkStmtFuelS_some_of_in_budget
  rw [single_set_binder_cost]
  exact h

/-- ONE BUDGET SEPARATES THE TWO RUNGS.  Take the budget that exactly affords
the one-binder shape: at any non-empty box the two-binder shape is strictly
over it, so a SINGLE ceiling answers the tractable rung and declines the
other.  That is the class measurement's split proved rather than tabulated,
and it is what makes a forall-side ceiling a re-pricing instead of a
refusal. -/
theorem one_budget_separates_the_two_rungs (box : List Int)
    (hbox : 0 < box.length) (k1 k2 j : Nat) (p : PdS)
    (senv : Nat -> Int -> Bool) (env : Nat -> Int) :
    checkStmtFuelS ((2 ^ box.length) * (box.length * 1)) box (subsetsOfS box)
        senv env (StmtS.ssallS k1 (StmtS.sallS j (StmtS.base p)))
      = some (checkStmtBoxS box (subsetsOfS box) senv env
          (StmtS.ssallS k1 (StmtS.sallS j (StmtS.base p))))
    /\ checkStmtFuelS ((2 ^ box.length) * (box.length * 1)) box
        (subsetsOfS box) senv env
        (StmtS.ssallS k1 (StmtS.ssallS k2 (StmtS.sallS j (StmtS.base p))))
      = none := by
  have hpos : 0 < (2 : Nat) ^ box.length * (box.length * 1) :=
    Nat.mul_pos (Nat.pos_pow_of_pos _ (by decide)) (by simpa using hbox)
  have hone : (1 : Nat) < 2 ^ box.length := by
    have h2 : (2 : Nat) ^ 1 <= 2 ^ box.length :=
      Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by decide) hbox
    exact Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide) h2
  constructor
  · exact single_set_binder_answers_in_budget box k1 j p senv env _ (Nat.le_refl _)
  · apply checkStmtFuelS_none_of_over_budget
    rw [lead_subject_cost_is_the_squared_powerset]
    calc (2 : Nat) ^ box.length * (box.length * 1)
        = 1 * (2 ^ box.length * (box.length * 1)) := by rw [Nat.one_mul]
      _ < (2 ^ box.length) * (2 ^ box.length * (box.length * 1)) :=
          Nat.mul_lt_mul_of_lt_of_le hone (Nat.le_refl _) hpos
